summary: The candidate correctly converts the reviewed sparse-metadata dense fallback into an explicit unsupported error and adds focused coverage. This is a partial fail-closed hardening only; it does not implement CompressedTensorsW4A16Sparse24.

tests.what_was_measured: Reproduced the original top-level ImportError, the unsafe dense WNA16 selection for mixed/per-group W4A16 with matching 2:4 metadata, and the unquantized unsupported error.
All three supplied counterexamples fail closed with explicit quantized or unquantized 2:4 unsupported errors.
Candidate regression suite: 9 passed and 2 subtests passed.
A dense-format 2:4 declaration fails closed; non-2:4 and nonmatching-target configurations continue to select dense WNA16.

gpu_evidence: The device was inventoried as AMD Instinct MI350X under ROCm 7.2, but the candidate contains no sparse execution implementation to run or compare numerically.
remaining_counterexamples: A valid top-level sparse-24-bitmask W4A16 checkpoint still raises ImportError instead of loading and executing a sparse scheme.
A mixed/per-group pack-quantized W4A16 checkpoint with matching 2:4 metadata now safely raises ImportError, but still cannot execute the requested sparse contract.
An unquantized 2:4 compressed-tensors checkpoint remains unsupported.
No CompressedTensorsW4A16Sparse24 scheme, sparse weight loader, or native execution kernel exists in the candidate.
remaining_limitations: The original sparse W4A16 feature is not implemented.
The assigned AMD architecture cannot validate a prospective NVIDIA sparse kernel, compiler output, or ISA.
No native source changed; a native rebuild was not applicable.
The 26B Gemma weights were unavailable, so full loading, NEXTN, HTTP serving, semantic accuracy, and sparse GPU numerics remain unverified.
The live checkpoint configuration was downloaded for configuration inspection only; it currently describes mixed FP8/NVFP4 and ignored vision projections, not proof of sparse support.
